outcome: Major CD identified on surface examination at birth
cohort: The study included 32,494 women with a viable pregnancy (>22 weeks gestation; birth weight >= 500 g) from the Western Cape Pregnancy Exposure Registry.
finding: The prevalence of major congenital defects identified on surface examination at birth was 7.2/1000 births, increasing to 9.2/1000 births when including missed/late diagnoses, and older maternal age and diabetes mellitus were associated with an increased prevalence.
followup_time: Up to 24 months (for assessment of late diagnoses), but primary prevalence measured at birth.
